title: SB0145 (110th General Assembly): As enacted, treats a licensed firearms dealer the same as a private citizen by allowing the dealer to occasionally sell, exchange, or transfer firearms from the dealer's personal collection without conducting a background check on the buyer; clarifies that the criminal history records check requirements do not apply to an occasional sale of a used or second-hand firearm by a person who is not engaged in the business of importing, manufacturing, or dealing in firearms. - Amends TCA Title 39, Chapter 17, Part 13.

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, Tennessee); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Tennessee text (Chaptered, 2017-04-28; same official document as TN-HB-61-2017.chaptered.txt (https://publications.tnsosfiles.com/acts/110/pub/pc0185.pdf); 2017-04-28)
provenance.note: Chaptered, Public Chapter 185 (2017-04-28), the law as enacted; text is the House bill HB 61's chapter, shared with SB 145. OCR text ('deale/s' for 'dealer's'). Section 1 rewrites subsection (l) listing transactions exempt from the background check; only the new (C) exemption is quoted. Effective on becoming law.

operative_text:
SECTION 1 (TCA 39-17-1316(l)(1)(C)): (C) Transactions by a gun dealer, as defined in subdivision (b)(2), making occasional sales, exchanges, or transfers of firearms that comprise all or part of the gun deale/s personal collection of firearms.
SECTION 2 (TCA 39-17-1316, new subsection): The criminal history records check required by this section shall not apply to an occasional sale of a used or second-hand firearm by a person who is not engaged in the business of importing, manufacturing, or dealing in firearms, pursuant to 18 U.S.C. SS 921 and 923.
